title: Middle East conflict threatens regional stability – Sajith
summary: By Naalir Jamaldeen Leader of the Opposition and Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) Sajith Premadasa has claimed that the escalating aggression and widening conflict across the Middle East pose a grave threat to regional stability and global peace due to the ongoing war between the USA–Israel alliance and Iran. Taking to X, Opposition Leader Premadasa stated that any expansion of hostilities—whether through attacks or destabilising actions targeting countries such as Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, or other nations in the region—must be unequivocally condemned. He added that the human cost of war is always the heaviest burden. Millions of civilians across the region face insecurity, displacement, and economic hardship. In particular, the safety and well-being of over one million Sri Lankans working in the Middle East remain a matter of profound concern. Their livelihoods support families back home and contribute significantly to Sri Lanka’s economy. Any further escalation would put innocent lives and vital economic stability at serious risk. Premadasa stressed that war rarely delivers lasting solutions. Dialogue, diplomacy, and negotiated settlements remain the only sustainable path forward. Immediate efforts towards ceasefire agreements, peace talks, and constructive negotiations are essential to prevent further suffering and regional destabilisation. He emphasised that the international community must act responsibly and urgently to prevent further military escalation, protect civilian populations and migrant workers, safeguard critical infrastructure and economic stability, and facilitate inclusive and credible peace negotiations. History has repeatedly shown that conflicts left unchecked grow more complex and destructive. The time to act for peace is now. War must be avoided at all costs. The protection of human life, regional stability, and global security demands restraint, courage, and a renewed commitment to diplomacy.

title: To prevent potential shortage: Govt must prepare alternative fuel plans – Attanayake
summary: By Naalir Jamaldeen Tissa Attanayake, National Organiser of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB), yesterday (3), urged the Government to prepare alternative plans to meet the country’s fuel demand once the current one-month stock runs out. Addressing the media in Colombo, Attanayake said that while the Government has assured the public of sufficient fuel stocks for a month, it must also be ready to prevent a potential shortage once those reserves are depleted. He noted that if adequate fuel stocks are available, the public need not panic. However, he cautioned that relying on imports from countries such as India and Singapore may not be a secure long-term solution, particularly if the ongoing conflict in the Middle East escalates and disrupts global fuel supplies. Attanayake stated that the SJB views the war in the Middle East with concern and hopes for its swift conclusion. He stressed that the Government must prioritise the safety and well-being of Sri Lankans employed in Middle Eastern countries. He highlighted several urgent matters requiring immediate attention, including protecting the lives and employment of Sri Lankan migrant workers in the Middle East, safeguarding foreign remittances sent by these workers, and ensuring the stability of tea exports, noting that nearly 25% of Sri Lanka’s tea exports are destined for Middle Eastern markets. Attanayake emphasised that it is the duty of the Opposition to advise the Government on properly managing national challenges. He rejected suggestions that such criticism amounts to political destabilisation. “As an Opposition party, we are obliged to point out mistakes with the aim of correcting them,” he said. He further clarified that the SJB does not encourage public unrest or fuel queues, instead urging citizens to avoid panic and conserve fuel where possible. title: Citing ‘serious safety risks’: U.S. citizens told to leave 14 Middle Eastern countries
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan The United States’ Department of State has urged Americans to immediately depart several countries in the Middle East using available commercial transportation, citing “serious safety risks” amid escalating tensions in the region. In a security update issued on 2 March, the department called on US citizens in affected areas to leave without delay and to make use of commercial travel options while they remain available. The advisory applies to Americans in Bahrain, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Israel, including the West Bank and Gaza, as well as Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen. “Depart now via commercial means due to serious safety risks,” the notice stated. Americans requiring assistance in arranging their departure have been advised to contact the State Department’s 24-hour helplines (from the United States and Canada). The US citizens were also encouraged to enrol in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Programme (STEP) to receive the latest security updates from the nearest US embassy or consulate.

title: WI wrap SL up for 308 despite Dhananjaya 120
summary: Dhananjaya de Silva’s commanding 120 off 168 deliveries was the backbone of Sri Lanka’s resistance on day one of the Test series against West Indies. His innings, full of authority and flair, helped the hosts recover from a shaky start after losing three wickets in the opening hour. Kemar Roach struck in the first over, before Alzarri Joseph removed two batters in three balls during the 10th over to leave Sri Lanka reeling at 42 for 3. On a surface offering assistance to the quicks, Sri Lanka clawed back through Dinesh Chandimal’s counterattacking half-century, followed by de Silva’s assured strokeplay across the middle and evening sessions. De Silva’s knock was built on three crucial partnerships: 68 with Chandimal, 99 with Sonal Dinusha, and 64 with Milan Rathnayaka. Dinusha’s restrained 43 off 75 balls provided valuable support, while Rathnayaka’s 27 ensured Sri Lanka crossed the 300 mark. Sri Lanka’s total of 308 was competitive rather than commanding. West Indies’ seamers — Roach, Alzarri, and Shamar Joseph — were consistently threatening, but it was Justin Greaves’ medium pace that proved decisive. He dismissed de Silva midway through the final session and added two tail-end scalps to finish with 3 for 39. Roach, Alzarri, and Shamar claimed two wickets apiece. West Indies faced one over before stumps and survived unscathed, though their over rate was sluggish, with only 72.5 overs bowled across six-and-a-half hours. De Silva’s innings sparkled with disdainful pulls and crisp drives. He repeatedly punished Alzarri Joseph, spanking him through point and then pulling him through square leg in the same over. Though frequently beaten on the outside edge, he kept the scoreboard ticking with singles and twos, while scoring heavily through cover and deep third. Dinusha, meanwhile, capitalized on short, wide deliveries, particularly through backward point. Soon after tea, de Silva reached his 13th Test century off 150 balls, bringing up the milestone with a stylish fli...

title: Athapaththu’s Record Blitz Powers Sri Lanka Women to Nine‑Wicket Win
summary: Skipper Chamari Athapaththu lit up Bristol with a blistering unbeaten 106 off just 61 deliveries, decorated with 17 fours and two sixes, as Sri Lanka Women cruised to a commanding nine‑wicket victory over Ireland Women in their T20 World Cup fixture today. This innings also marked herfourth T20I century, underlining her status as one of the most destructive batters in women’s cricket. Ireland Women were restricted to 130 for 5, with Gaby Lewis top‑scoring with 59 and Alice Tector adding 28. Sri Lanka chased down the target in only 15.3 overs, losing just one wicket, thanks to Athapaththu’s special innings. Imesha Dulani provided solid support with 20 runs. Scores: Ireland Women: 130/5 (20.0 ) (Gaby Lewis 59, Alice Tector 28) Sri Lanka Women: 134/1 (15.3 ) ( Chamari Athapaththu 106* , Imesha Dulani 20)

title: Tharanga Dominates Doha with 88.68m Monster Throw
Rumesh Tharanga Climbs to World No. 2 After Ostrava Triumph
summary: Following another monster throw in Ostrava yesterday, Sri Lanka’s javelin sensation Rumesh Tharanga Pathiragae has climbed to second place in the World Athletics rankings, moving up from third. Germany’s Julian Weber continues to lead with 1360 points, while Tharanga now sits close behind on 1333 points. In 2026, Tharanga has been nothing short of dominant, registering all of the top four throws of the year — an unprecedented achievement for a Sri Lankan athlete in any discipline. The 23‑year‑old, trained under Tony Prasanna, continued his golden run in Europe by clinching gold at the Ostrava Golden Spike competition in the Czech Republic with a throw of 86.57m. Competing in this World Athletics Continental Tour Gold event, he opened with 85.87m, improved to 86.30m on his second attempt, and sealed victory with 86.57m on his third. That effort was more than enough to secure the top spot. Double World Champion Anderson Peters of Grenada finished second with 84.27m, while South Africa’s Douw Smit claimed third with 83.90m. Earlier this month in Rome, Tharanga stunned the athletics world with a throw of 92.62m, making him the 8th best thrower of all time. In Ostrava, unlike Rome, he entered as the clear favorite  the “man to beat” in world javelin this year. He was even featured as the face of the competition during the pre‑event press conference alongside US Olympic pole vault champion Katie Moon. Currently ranked second in the world, Tharanga owns the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5th best throws of the season. He is the first Sri Lankan athlete in history to achieve such a high global ranking in a specific event, marking a new era of dominance for Sri Lankan athletics. Following Ostrava, Tharanga will compete in the Diamond League in Doha before returning home. Next month, he is set to represent Sri Lanka at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland, where expectations will be sky‑high.

title: Ananda Ends 23-Year Wait with Historic Victory Over St. Thomas’ College
summary: Ananda College Rugby produced one of the most memorable moments in the school’s sporting history by defeating St. Thomas’ College and ending a 23-year wait for victory over the Mount Lavinia outfit in the Schools Rugby League encounter played at Rajagiriya. The landmark triumph is more than just a win. It is the latest chapter in a remarkable resurgence that has transformed Ananda into one of the most courageous and competitive teams in Division ‘A’ rugby this season. Having returned to the top division after a lengthy absence, many observers expected Ananda to struggle against the established powerhouses. Instead, the Maroon and Gold warriors have earned admiration across the rugby fraternity for their fearless approach, commitment, and fighting spirit. Week after week, they have challenged stronger and more experienced opponents, refusing to be intimidated by reputation or history. This victory over St. Thomas’ is a fitting reward for a team that has consistently punched above its weight throughout the season. While the league table may not fully reflect their performances, several narrow defeats in the opening weeks denied Ananda the opportunity of securing a place in the Cup Segment. Those close losses, often decided by the finest of margins, masked the true quality of this young side. Many rugby followers would agree that based on performances alone, Ananda deserved to be among the Cup Segment contenders. The team’s ability to compete with the best schools in the country, despite being newcomers to Division ‘A’, has been one of the stories of the 2026 season. The victory against St. Thomas’ also underlines the remarkable progress achieved by the coaching staff, management, players, and supporters who have worked tirelessly to rebuild the rugby programme. What has stood out most is the character of the players. Time and again they have shown resilience, determination, and an unwavering belief in their ability to compete at the highest level. title: Shanaka, Mishara fifties set up series-levelling win for Sri Lanka
summary: Dasun Shanaka produced the batting ballistics, Kamil Mishara held the innings together, and Sri Lanka’s spinners dominated the middle overs, comfortably defending their 194 for 6. This 37-run victory brings Sri Lanka level 1-1 in the series against West Indies, with one match to play on Sunday night. Sri Lanka had been struggling at 88 for 4 in the 13th over when Shanaka joined Mishara at the crease. The pair then blasted 103 off 42 balls together to propel Sri Lanka to a commanding score of 194 for 6, hitting seven sixes and nine fours between them. Although Sri Lanka struck twice with the new ball, West Indies had still looked confident in pursuit at 89 for 2, until Sri Lanka’s spinners went to work. A run out would spark a collapse that cost West Indies six wickets for 32 runs. They struggled to recover from 122 for 8 after 15 overs. Dushmantha Chameera, who had struck early in the innings and was effective in the other phases as well, closed out the match in the 19th over, taking three wickets for 9 runs. West Indies were 157 all out, despite Rovman Powell and Shimron Hetmyer having put on 81 off 47 for the third wicket. Although he arrived at the crease with Sri Lanka in some trouble, Shanaka was almost immediately aggressive, blasting Roston Chase’s offspin onto the roof of the Sabina Park stadium fourth ball, before crashing him for a four and thumping another six next ball. All three of these boundaries came through deep midwicket. He also struck a huge six down the ground, and hooked a ball over fine leg as well, as he stormed to a 19-ball fifty. title: Rumesh to Compete in Ostrava on Tuesday
summary: By Anjana Kaluarachchi After his heroic performance in Rome that made world headlines, javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga will head to the Czech Republic to compete in the Golden Ostrava on Tuesday, 16 June, a World Athletics Continental Tour Gold event. Tharanga, who threw 92.62m to become the 8thbest thrower of all time, will once again face double world champion Anderson Peters of Grenada and former Olympic gold medalist Thomas Röhler of Germany, among other top competitors. Unlike in Rome, Rumesh will enter the competition as the favorite, carrying the tag of ‘man to beat’ in world javelin this year. The 23-year-old former Peterite is currently ranked third in the world and owns the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5thbest throws of the season. He is the first Sri Lankan athlete in history to achieve such a high global ranking in a specific event, marking a new level of world dominance for Sri Lankan athletics. Following his heroic performance in Rome, Tharanga stayed in Italy for a week, training in both Rome and Milan, before departing for the Czech Republic yesterday. Following Ostrava, Tharanga will compete in the Diamond League in Doha before returning to Sri Lanka. Next month, he will head to Scotland to represent the country at the Commonwealth Games.

title: SL Star Rumesh Tharanga Rises to 3rd in World Rankings
summary: Sri Lanka’s javelin sensation Rumesh Tharanga has stunned the athletics world, rising to third place in the global javelin throw rankings after his monster throw of 92.62m at the Rome Diamond League. With that performance, Tharanga has now amassed 1,324 ranking points, placing him just behind Germany’s Julian Weber and Grenada’s Anderson Peters. Notably, he is the youngest athlete in the world’s top 20, underscoring his rapid rise and extraordinary potential. A Historic Milestone for Sri Lanka Tharanga’s achievement marks a historic milestone for Sri Lankan athletics, as he becomes the highest-ranked male athlete from the nation in world athletics standings. He has also emerged as Asia’s top-ranked javelin thrower, overtaking India’s Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra. The 23-year-old’s record-breaking performance in Rome  not only secured his maiden Diamond League victory but also set a new national record, a meet record, and reaffirmed his position as the world leader this season. Historic Throw in Rome Just days after making his Diamond League debut in Rabat, where he finished second, Tharanga soared past the 90m mark for the first time in Rome. title: Chamari, Vishmi Power Sri Lanka to Comfortable Win over Pakistan
summary: Skipper Chamari Athapaththu fell just short of what could have been a magnificent century, but her blistering 94 ensured Sri Lanka cruised to a comfortable victory over Pakistan in their ICC Women’s T20 World Cup warm-up match at Derby today. Pakistan, batting first, posted 168 for 8, with Chethana Vimukthi starring for Sri Lanka’s bowling attack by claiming 4 for 31. In reply, Athapaththu and 20 year old Vishmi Gunarathne forged a commanding 159-run opening stand that all but sealed the game. Athapaththu, attempting to reach her century with a six, was dismissed for 94 off 58 balls  an innings decorated with nine fours and five sixes. Gunarathne, who showed intent early in the powerplay with a flurry of boundaries, remained unbeaten on 63 from 50 deliveries, striking four fours and three sixes. Her composed knock perfectly complemented Athapaththu’s fireworks, guiding Sri Lanka to a dominant finish.
